description: A halal screening platform that checks whether stocks and other investments meet Islamic guidelines. In September 2026 it teamed up with Asal Invest to supply that screening data to investors across the US. No official company website could be verified; it appears to be a young company covered so far only in Islamic finance trade press.
name: RihalQ

sources.label: IFN Investor monthly review (Sept 2026) — notes RihalQ's partnership with Asal Invest

description: A large US investment firm that manages money for pension funds, governments, and other big investors, focusing on private markets like private equity and private lending. It is listed on the Nasdaq stock exchange under the ticker STEP.
name: StepStone Group

description: A fund manager based in Dubai's financial district (DIFC) and controlled by Al Salam Bank, which handles money for investors across the Middle East. In October 2026 it partnered with StepStone Group to launch a private financing fund.
name: ASB Capital

description: A US-based registered investment adviser that manages money and gives financial advice to clients. In September 2026 it partnered with RihalQ to get Islamic screening data for its US investors.
name: Asal Invest

sources.label: IFN Investor monthly review (Sept 2026) — notes the Asal Invest / RihalQ partnership

description: An investment company based in the United Arab Emirates that puts money into property, private businesses, and other opportunities while following Islamic rules. It manages more than $4 billion for investors and in October 2026 bought a majority stake in London House Exchange.
name: Gulf Islamic Investments

description: A UK platform that lets people buy small slices of rental properties and trade them on a regulated exchange, instead of having to buy a whole house. It started life as Property Partner and is overseen by the UK's Financial Conduct Authority.
name: London House Exchange

description: A UK finance company that offers home-buying and buy-to-let products built on Islamic co-ownership, so there is no interest charge. It grew fast after Gulf Islamic Investments took a majority stake, and in 2026 it bought Bank of Ireland's Alburaq Islamic home finance portfolio.
name: Offa

sources.label: FF News — Offa's buy-to-let rate announcement, referencing the Alburaq acquisition

description: An app-based investing platform that builds portfolios only from halal stocks, Islamic bonds (sukuk), and gold, with scholars checking that everything stays within Islamic rules. It serves hundreds of thousands of customers in the US, UK, Malaysia, and other countries.
name: Wahed

description: A small Seattle-based investment firm that filed with US regulators to launch an Islamic exchange-traded fund tracking large American stocks, advised by Exchange Traded Concepts and Mellon Capital with the Shariyah Review Bureau as its Islamic adviser. No official company website could be verified.
name: Falah Capital

sources.label: Reuters (via LSE) — Seattle-based Falah Capital is preparing an Islamic ETF (Oct 2026)

description: An investment manager based in Bellingham, Washington, that runs the Amana mutual funds — some of the oldest Islamic mutual funds in the United States. It picks stocks and bonds that pass Islamic screening so observant Muslims can invest with a clear conscience.
name: Saturna Capital

sources.label: SEC — Amana fund documents naming Saturna Capital Corporation as investment adviser

description: Germany's first Islamic bank, based in Frankfurt and owned by Turkey's Kuveyt Turk participation bank. It offers accounts, savings, and financing for individuals and businesses using profit-sharing instead of interest.
name: KT Bank AG

description: New York-based global alternative investment manager (~$30B AUM); its Global Sukuk Team won Euromoney's World's Best Islamic Fund Manager 2026.
name: Wafra Inc.

description: Islamic investment certificates. Instead of lending money and collecting interest (which is riba), sukuk holders own a share of a real asset or project — like an airport terminal — and earn returns from the profit it generates. Often called 'Islamic bonds,' but they are ownership certificates, not debt.
name: Sukuk

description: How an ETF holding Apple or Microsoft can be halal: the fund tracks an index of stocks screened against Islamic rules — no interest-based income, no alcohol, gambling or arms businesses, and strict limits on debt. A Shariah board certifies compliance, and any small leftover non-compliant income is 'purified' by donating it to charity.
name: Islamic ETFs and Shariah stock screening

description: Loans made directly to companies by non-bank lenders (like investment funds) instead of through a bank. It has been one of the fastest-growing corners of conventional finance; Shariah-compliant versions structure the lending without interest — for example through cost-plus sales or profit-sharing deals.
name: Private credit

sources.label: Alternative Credit Investor: ASB StepStone fund

description: Owning a small slice of an expensive asset — like a fraction of a rental property — instead of buying the whole thing. Regulated exchanges now let everyday investors buy and sell these slices, which fits Islamic finance naturally since returns come from a real asset you partly own.
name: Fractional ownership

sources.label: Alternative Credit Investor: GII / London House Exchange

name: SP Funds
description: The ETF arm of the ShariaPortfolio group. It runs a small lineup of US-listed halal exchange-traded funds — including the S&P Global Technology ETF that topped IFN Investor's America league table by three-month returns on October 5, 2026.

name: ShariaPortfolio
description: A US boutique asset manager (registered investment adviser with the SEC) that has offered Shariah-compliant investing since 2003. Its group of companies manages over $3 billion and includes the SP Funds halal ETF lineup, plus wealth management and advisory services.

name: Euroclear
description: A Brussels-based financial-market infrastructure group that settles and safekeeps securities for banks and investors worldwide. In October 2026, Qatar chose Euroclear Bank to settle its riyal-denominated government bonds and sukuk for international investors — the first time global buyers could access them this way.

sources.label: Salaam Gateway — Qatar links government bonds and sukuk to Euroclear

name: Dubai Islamic Bank
description: The UAE's largest Islamic bank by assets and the world's first full-service Islamic bank, founded in 1975. In October 2026 it announced it would redeem its outstanding $500 million Additional Tier 1 sukuk on its first call date, October 19, 2026.

sources.label: Reuters via TradingView — DIB to redeem $500m AT1 sukuk (Oct 7, 2026)

name: Euronext Dublin
description: Ireland's main stock exchange and a common listing venue for international debt securities and sukuk, including Gulf issuers. Dubai Islamic Bank's $500 million AT1 sukuk was listed here until its planned redemption in October 2026.

sources.label: Reuters via TradingView — DIB to redeem $500m AT1 sukuk (Oct 7, 2026)

name: Murabaha
description: A 'cost-plus' sale used across Islamic finance. The bank buys an asset (a house, car, or machine) and sells it to the customer at a disclosed price — its cost plus an agreed profit markup — paid in fixed installments. Because the bank genuinely buys and then sells the asset, this counts as trade rather than an interest-bearing loan. Example: halal home financing, where the bank buys a house and resells it to the buyer at a fixed marked-up price paid over years.

sources.label: Islamic Finance Daily Brief — Learn section (Oct 8, 2026)

name: Additional Tier 1 (AT1) sukuk
description: A type of bank funding that sits between equity and ordinary debt: it can absorb losses if the bank gets into trouble, and the bank can usually redeem (call) it on a set date. Dubai Islamic Bank's $500 million AT1 sukuk, issued in 2021, is the Shariah-compliant version of this instrument — called on its first call date, October 19, 2026.

sources.label: Reuters via TradingView — DIB to redeem $500m AT1 sukuk (Oct 7, 2026)

name: Short interest
description: The total number of a stock's (or ETF's) shares that investors have borrowed and sold, betting the price will fall. A rise in short interest means more traders are taking that side of the bet. Example: short interest in Wahed's HLAL halal ETF jumped 66% during September 2026 — though at under 1% of shares, it was still a small position.

sources.label: Defense World — Wahed FTSE USA Shariah ETF short interest (Oct 2, 2026)

name: Wafra
description: A New York-based asset manager with about $30 billion under management. Its Global Sukuk Strategy, an actively managed portfolio of Islamic bonds, was named World's Best Islamic Fund Manager at the 2026 Euromoney Islamic Finance Awards — its third win in a row.

sources.label: PR Newswire: Wafra named World's Best Islamic Fund Manager 2026

name: Baruch Islamic Investment Research Group
description: A student-run investment research group at Baruch College in New York. It was a featured organizer of the inaugural student-led Islamic Finance Conference in September 2026, part of a growing student-built Islamic finance ecosystem in the city.

sources.label: World City Press: Baruch College Islamic Finance Conference

name: Euromoney
description: A financial media and events company. Its annual Islamic Finance Awards, judged by its journalists and researchers, recognize the year's strongest Islamic finance institutions — Wafra won Best Islamic Fund Manager in 2026.

sources.label: PR Newswire: Wafra named World's Best Islamic Fund Manager 2026

name: MASNA Ventures
description: A Saudi venture capital firm behind the Sentinel Shield Fund I, a defense-tech fund backing the local manufacture of advanced technologies in Saudi Arabia. In October 2026 it appointed Al Marji Advisory for independent Sharia governance of the fund.

sources.label: mid-east.info — Sentinel Shield Fund I appoints Al Marji Advisory (Oct 2026)

name: Al Marji Advisory Company
description: A Riyadh-based Sharia advisory firm that helps Islamic financial institutions meet Sharia governance rules. In October 2026 it was appointed to set up and supervise the Sharia board for MASNA Ventures' Sentinel Shield Fund I, including audits and certification.

sources.label: mid-east.info — Sentinel Shield Fund I appoints Al Marji Advisory (Oct 2026)

name: j. awan capital
description: A Riyadh-based fund manager that runs MASNA Ventures' Sentinel Shield Fund I, a Saudi-regulated defense venture capital fund. It structures and manages the fund's investments in unmanned systems, AI-enabled defense, and related technologies.

sources.label: mid-east.info — Sentinel Shield Fund I appoints Al Marji Advisory (Oct 2026)

name: Devon Bank
description: A Chicago community bank running one of the oldest Islamic finance programs in the US. It offers Sharia-compliant home financing (murabaha) and profit-sharing deposit accounts, giving American Muslims an alternative to interest-based banking.

name: University Islamic Financial
description: A Michigan-based Islamic finance provider (a subsidiary of University Bank) offering Sharia-compliant home financing through murabaha and ijara structures, plus halal deposit accounts. One of the first Islamic banking operations in the US.

name: Sharia board
description: A panel of Islamic scholars that checks whether a bank's or fund's products and deals follow Islamic rules. Example: Al Marji Advisory was hired to set up and supervise an independent Sharia board for the Sentinel Shield Fund I.

sources.label: Oct 9 edition — Sentinel Shield Fund I story

name: Special-purpose vehicle (SPV)
description: A separate legal company created to hold specific assets or investments, keeping them apart from the parent firm's other business. Example: the Sentinel Shield Fund I invests through SPVs focused on areas like unmanned systems and AI-enabled defense.

sources.label: Oct 9 edition — Sentinel Shield Fund I story

name: Halal robo-advisor
description: An online service that builds and manages your investment portfolio automatically, using only Shariah-compliant investments. Example: Wahed, the largest halal robo-advisor for US investors, offers six risk levels from a $100 minimum.

name: Manzil
description: An Islamic fintech whose US arm (Manzil Invest USA, an SEC-registered adviser) launched a Shariah-compliant trading app in July 2026 built on Alpaca brokerage APIs with Zoya screening integrated.

sources.label: EIN Presswire — Manzil trading platform launch (Jul 2026)

name: Alpaca
description: An API-first brokerage infrastructure company (FINRA member, SIPC-insured) that lets fintech apps offer stock trading without building a brokerage. Example: Manzil's halal trading app runs its trade execution and custody on Alpaca.

sources.label: EIN Presswire — Manzil trading platform launch (Jul 2026)

name: Zoya
description: A Shariah stock-screening service used by US Muslim investors and fintech apps. Example: Manzil integrated Zoya directly into its trading app for real-time compliance reports against AAOIFI standards.

sources.label: EIN Presswire — Manzil trading platform launch (Jul 2026)

name: iRizq
description: A US-based halal investing education platform that teaches a halal value-investing framework and provides Shariah stock-screening tools built by co-founder Sarfaraz Nasir.

name: Arab National Bank
description: A major bank based in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia (founded 1979, listed on the Saudi Stock Exchange), offering conventional and Shariah-compliant retail, corporate and investment banking, with branches in Saudi Arabia and the UK.

name: Islamic Financial Literacy Month
description: An annual October initiative by Saturna Capital that promotes Islamic financial education through in-person seminars and online webinars on topics such as halal retirement investing. Example: its October 14, 2026 webinar on keeping 401(k)s and IRAs halal.

name: 401(k) and IRA
description: US retirement accounts where the government lets your savings grow with less tax as long as the money stays inside the account. For Muslim savers, the default investments inside many employer plans (bond or money-market funds) earn interest, so the picks often need switching to Shariah-screened funds.

sources.label: Saturna Capital — Islamic Financial Literacy Month

name: Ayan Capital
description: A London fintech offering halal car finance across the UK through an Ijara wa Iqtina (lease-to-own) model, with no interest. In September 2026 it secured a $100 million Shariah-compliant facility as it prepares a UK banking licence application on its way to a full halal digital bank.

sources.label: PR Newswire — Ayan Capital secures $100M facility (Sep 2026)

name: Triple Point
description: A London-based alternative investment manager. In September 2026 it originated the senior Shariah-compliant facility of up to $100 million funding Ayan Capital's halal car finance growth.

sources.label: PR Newswire — Ayan Capital secures $100M facility (Sep 2026)

name: Ijara wa Iqtina
description: A lease-to-own contract used in Islamic finance. The financier buys the asset and stays its legal owner while the customer pays fixed rent; ownership transfers at the end of the term. Because the payment is rent rather than loan repayment, no interest is involved. Example: Ayan Capital's halal car finance in the UK.

sources.label: PR Newswire — Ayan Capital secures $100M facility (Sep 2026)

name: Accredited investor
description: In the US, an investor the SEC lets into private investments that are not open to the public: income above $200,000 a year ($300,000 with a spouse), net worth above $1 million excluding the home, or certain finance licences.

name: Zakat on investments
description: Zakat is the yearly obligation to give 2.5% of qualifying wealth to charity, and investments count as wealth. For stocks and funds held as a long-term investment, most scholars say you pay on the market value on your zakat due date; traders pay on the full market value of holdings treated as trade goods. Retirement accounts such as a 401(k) also count, though some scholars allow delaying payment until withdrawal.

sources.label: Amal Invest — how much zakat to pay on stocks

name: Purification
description: Purification means giving away the small haram income inside an otherwise halal investment, instead of keeping it. Even screened companies and funds can earn a little interest on cash balances, and Shariah standards tolerate up to 5% of revenue from such sources. Investors donate that impure portion of their dividends to charity. It is separate from zakat: zakat is the obligation on wealth, purification cleans income you should not have kept.

sources.label: HalalWallet — why tech stocks land in 'questionable' and how investors handle purification

name: Riba
description: Riba means interest: any guaranteed extra charged for the use of money. It is prohibited in the Quran and is the main dividing line between Islamic and conventional finance. Islamic finance replaces interest with shared risk — the financier shares in profit, charges rent for an asset, or sells goods at a price paid over time — so returns come from real economic activity.

name: Nomo
description: A UK-based Shariah-compliant digital bank, part of BLME (Bank of London and The Middle East). It offers app-based banking and investments, including professionally managed Shariah-compliant portfolios through Nomo Investments.

name: Allfunds
description: A Spain-headquartered fund distribution platform that connects fund managers with banks and wealth managers. It gives partners like Nomo access to a wide shelf of investment funds through a single connection.

name: Mudaraba
description: A partnership where one side provides the capital (rabb al-mal) and the other provides the work and skill (mudarib). Profits are split by an agreed percentage; losses fall on the capital provider, while the manager loses their effort — unless they were negligent. Islamic banks use it for savings accounts, with depositors as capital providers and the bank as manager.

name: 52-week high
description: The highest price a stock or fund has traded at over the past year. When the halal ETF SPUS reached $60.49 in October 2026, it marked a new 52-week high — meaning buyers were paying more than at any point in the previous twelve months.

sources.label: The Cerbat Gem: SPUS sets new 1-year high

name: AlBaraka Forum for Islamic Economy
description: An independent, non-profit global think tank focused on the Islamic economy, continuing the work of its founder Sheikh Saleh Abdullah Kamel. It organises the annual AlBaraka Summit, whose 5th edition met in London in October 2026.

sources.label: PR Newswire — London summit day-one outcomes (Oct 13, 2026)

name: Expense ratio
description: The yearly fee for owning a fund, shown as a percentage of your investment — for example, a 0.50% expense ratio costs $50 a year on $10,000. It is taken from the fund's assets, so you never see a separate bill. Halal funds often charge more than broad market funds because screening and audits add costs.

name: Sukuk redemption (call)
description: When a sukuk issuer buys back its certificates on a call date named in the original terms, paying holders full face value plus any profit payments still owed. The certificates then stop trading and the listing is cancelled. A redemption is a planned contract step, different from a default, where the issuer fails to pay.

name: Islamic Development Bank (IsDB)
description: A development bank owned by 57 Muslim-majority countries, based in Jeddah. It finances roads, hospitals, schools, farms, and businesses using Shariah-compliant methods like leasing and installment sales instead of interest-based lending.

name: International Fund for Agricultural Development (IFAD)
description: A UN agency that finances farming and rural communities in developing countries. On Oct 14, 2026 it signed a $750 million co-financing deal with the Islamic Development Bank for food systems and rural transformation.

name: M-Pesa
description: A mobile money service started in Kenya in 2007. It lets people send money, pay bills, and save using a basic mobile phone with no bank account. About 41 million people use it.

name: Money market fund
description: A fund that pools money from many small investors and puts it into very short-term, very safe instruments. The aim is to keep your capital safe while earning a small steady return, and you can withdraw any day. A Shariah version only uses halal instruments.

name: Erad
description: A Riyadh-based fintech that gives Shariah-compliant working capital to small businesses. Its AI models study a business's cash flow to approve financing in about 48 hours. It raised $22 million in September 2026 and has lent over $133 million to date.

name: Guidance Residential
description: The largest US provider of Islamic home financing, based in Reston, Virginia. It uses a Declining Balance Co-ownership program: buyer and company buy the home together, and the buyer gradually acquires the company's share with monthly payments instead of paying interest. It says it has funded over $4.9 billion in Shariah-compliant home financing.

sources.label: The Times of Texas — Guidance Residential's co-ownership program and $4.9B funded

name: IjaraCDC
description: Ijara Community Development Corporation, a Michigan-based nonprofit that structures Shariah-compliant home financing across the USA and Canada. It uses the Ijara lease-to-own model and works through licensed financing providers rather than lending itself.

sources.label: IjaraCDC — about its Ijara lease-to-own home financing model

name: Ijara
description: An Islamic lease contract: one party owns an asset and the other pays fixed monthly rent to use it, with no interest. In the lease-to-own form (ijara wa iqtina), each payment is split between rent and a contribution toward ownership, so the user ends up owning the asset at the end of the term.

sources.label: Islamic Finance Daily Brief — Oct 16, 2026 edition (Ijara explainer)

name: Sukuk programme
description: A pre-approved framework letting an issuer sell sukuk in multiple tranches up to a set ceiling, instead of arranging each sale from scratch. Example: OQEP's $2B programme lets the Omani energy company issue tranches whenever market conditions suit.

name: Municipal sukuk
description: Sukuk issued by a city or municipal government to fund public services or refinance existing debt. Example: Greater Amman Municipality's JD400M ijara sukuk — Jordan's first — to replace expensive conventional loans.

name: HSBC
description: A British multinational bank headquartered in London. It runs the HSBC Islamic Global Equity Index Fund, one of the largest Shariah-screened equity funds, which sits inside most UK halal workplace pension schemes.

sources.label: Media Review Network — HSBC sharia-compliant fund holdings report (Oct 2026)

name: Tokenised sukuk
description: A sukuk whose ownership is recorded as digital tokens on a shared ledger (blockchain) instead of a paper registry. The Shariah structure underneath is unchanged; tokenisation changes the record-keeping and can cut the investment into small pieces so ordinary people can buy in. Example: Malaysia's planned retail tokenised government sukuk under Budget 2027.

sources.label: LEMON Blog — Malaysia plans tokenised government sukuk for retail investors (Oct 2026)

name: Istisna
description: A contract to manufacture or build something that does not exist yet, to the buyer's specifications, with the price and delivery date fixed in advance. There is no interest and no loan. Example: an Islamic bank commissions a contractor to build a house on a customer's plot, pays the builder as work progresses, and the customer pays the bank in instalments.

name: Almalia
description: An international financial services group behind the Almalia Sanlam Active Shariah Global Equity UCITS ETF, the first actively managed global Shariah equity ETF on the London Stock Exchange.

name: Sanlam Investments
description: A South African-owned asset manager whose UK Global High Quality equity team runs the portfolio of the Almalia Shariah ETF.

name: HANetf
description: A European white-label ETF platform that handles the listing and fund mechanics for issuers like Almalia; the Almalia Shariah ETF is its tenth ETF.

name: Amanie Advisors
description: A Shariah advisory firm whose panel of scholars checks that the Almalia Shariah ETF holdings stay compliant with Islamic investment principles.

name: Zetrix AI
description: A Malaysian technology company (formerly MYEG) whose Sukuk Wakalah breached a covenant in October 2026, with RM2.0 billion in principal at risk.

name: Cashku
description: A Malaysian digital wealth platform (operated by licensed firm Advisonomics) offering Shariah-compliant funds, including sukuk and private credit funds, with tiny minimums and no sales charges.

name: Muamalat Invest
description: The Islamic fund management arm of Bank Muamalat Malaysia; its Shariah-compliant funds are distributed through the Cashku app.

name: Central Bank of Somalia
description: Somalia’s central bank, which joined AAOIFI in October 2026, committing its Islamic banking sector to international Shariah standards.

sources.label: Central Bank of Somalia official site

name: Actively managed ETF
description: An exchange-traded fund where professionals pick the stocks instead of copying an index. The Almalia Shariah ETF on the London Stock Exchange is the first actively managed global Shariah equity ETF.

name: Sukuk covenant
description: A promise written into a sukuk’s terms, such as keeping enough cash on hand. Breaking it is a breach that can lead to a waiver vote or a dissolution event.

name: Dissolution event (sukuk)
description: The sukuk equivalent of a default. If triggered, the trustee can accelerate: every outstanding sum becomes due immediately. Example: Zetrix AI’s Sukuk Wakalah, with RM2.0 billion in principal at risk.

name: Waqf
description: A permanent charitable endowment in Islamic law. The assets are locked in forever and only their income is spent, for example to fund mosques, schools, or scholars.

name: Salam
description: A contract for buying goods in advance: the buyer pays the full price now for goods delivered later, with goods, quantity, price, and delivery date fixed in the contract. Example: an Islamic bank paying a wheat farmer at planting time for delivery after harvest.

name: SkyWorld
description: A Malaysian property developer building high-rise residential, commercial, and affordable housing (its SkyAwani series) in Kuala Lumpur and Penang. In October 2026 its financing arm set up a MYR2 billion Sukuk Wakalah programme and issued the first MYR40 million.

name: Al Mal Capital REIT
description: A real estate investment trust listed on the Dubai Financial Market, investing in income-generating UAE and Gulf properties such as schools, healthcare, and industrial assets. It borrows through Shariah-compliant Corporate Ijarah facilities instead of conventional loans.

sources.label: Al Mal Capital REIT official site

name: RAK Bank
description: A UAE bank (the National Bank of Ras Al Khaimah) offering retail, business, and Islamic banking through its RAKislamic division. In October 2026 Al Mal Capital REIT sought unitholder approval to take an Islamic banking facility from it.

name: Sharjah Islamic Bank
description: A UAE Islamic bank offering Shariah-compliant retail, corporate, and investment banking. In October 2026 it was named as the bank ready to join a Pakistani sovereign sukuk issuance discussed at the World Bank-IMF meetings in Bangkok.

name: Wakala
description: An agency contract: an investor appoints an agent (wakil) to invest money under an agreed set of rules, for a fixed fee. Profits belong to the investor. Example: SkyWorld's Sukuk Wakalah, where investors appoint SkyWorld Capital as their agent to fund property development.

name: Panda bonds
description: Bonds sold in China by a foreign borrower, denominated in yuan. They let a country borrow from Chinese investors instead of only dollar markets. Example: Pakistan's RMB 7.2 billion Panda bond programme, first issued in May 2026.

name: Islamic REIT
description: A real estate investment trust that follows Shariah rules: it owns income-generating property, avoids interest-bearing debt, and keeps tenants in permissible businesses. Investors earn from rental income. Example: Al Mal Capital REIT on the Dubai Financial Market, which finances its properties with Corporate Ijarah facilities.

name: Arada Developments
description: UAE property developer building large residential and mixed-use communities in Sharjah and Dubai.

name: Nest
description: The UK's state-backed workplace pension scheme, open to any employer; its members' retirement savings include Sharia-compliant fund options.

name: Tender offer
description: When a company offers to buy back its own bonds or sukuk certificates from investors for cash, usually to refinance on better terms. Example: Arada's October 2026 offer to buy back $411.7 million of its 2027 sukuk at face value.

name: Google
description: Technology company behind the world's most-used search engine and a major ad platform. Its Financial Services Verification program screens finance advertisers, including halal home-finance providers, before their ads can run; it reaches the US and Canada in early 2027.

name: Equi
description: UK think tank producing ethically driven research on UK issues, drawing on Muslim insight. Its October 2026 'Have Faith in Higher Education' report put a £450 million price on introducing interest-free alternative student finance.

name: Financial Services Verification
description: Google's program that requires financial-services advertisers to prove they are authorized by a regulator or a recognized registry before their ads can run. It started in the UK in 2021 and reaches the US and Canada in early 2027. Example: a halal mortgage provider advertising on Google will need to show its licence.

name: Alternative student finance
description: The UK's planned interest-free student finance product, built on the Islamic principle of takaful: students receive tuition and living-cost payments from a mutual fund and later pay contributions into it, ringfenced for future students, with no interest.

name: Takaful (mutual support)
description: The Islamic principle of mutual support: a group pools contributions into a shared fund that pays out when members need it. The UK's planned alternative student finance uses a takaful fund — graduates' contributions pay for future students, with no interest involved.

name: Bank Negara Malaysia
description: Malaysia's central bank. In October 2026 it launched SSDS+, a distributed-ledger platform for issuing and holding tokenized bonds, including sukuk, that settles payments in central bank money around the clock.

name: The Alternative Bank (alt bank)
description: A Nigerian bank that operates entirely on non-interest (Islamic) finance principles. It started as a non-interest window inside Sterling Bank in 2014 and became a standalone licensed bank in 2023. In October 2026 it moved all its services onto MIZAN, a core banking platform built for Islamic finance.

name: Peerless
description: A Nigerian financial software firm. It built MIZAN, a core banking platform designed from the ground up for Islamic and non-interest financial institutions, with contract templates for Murabaha, Ijara, Mudaraba, Istisna, and Qard Hassan.

name: Tokenized bond
description: A bond recorded as a digital token on a shared ledger instead of in a traditional securities depository. Ownership changes when the token moves, and payment can settle at the same time. A tokenized sukuk still needs the same asset-backed structure and Shariah approvals as a conventional one — only the record-keeping changes.

name: Islamic core banking platform
description: Banking software built around Islamic contracts from the start. Conventional systems assume loans with interest; an Islamic core records who owns the asset at each step, rental schedules, and profit-sharing ratios. Example: Nigeria's Peerless built MIZAN, and alt bank moved all its services onto it in October 2026.

name: Bank Muamalat
description: Malaysia's second full-fledged Islamic bank, operating since 1999. In October 2026 it launched the Awwal Credit Card-i, a Shariah-compliant credit card with a 14% annual profit rate, no annual fee, and a non-compounding profit concept.

name: Islamic credit card
description: A credit card that follows Shariah principles: the bank charges no interest. Instead it earns a profit rate on balances the customer carries over. Some, like Bank Muamalat's 2026 Awwal Card-i, use non-compounding profit — profit is charged only on what the customer owes, never on profit added in earlier months.

name: S&P Dow Jones Indices
description: The company behind the S&P 500 and Dow Jones indexes. It also runs the main Shariah-screened stock indexes used around the world, including the S&P Global BMI Shariah and the Dow Jones Islamic Market indexes, and publishes quarterly reviews of how they perform.

name: Digital Nasional Berhad
description: The Malaysian company that built the country's wholesale 5G network and sells 5G access to mobile operators. In October 2026 it closed a MYR5.2 billion Islamic financing to fund the network, with the finance ministry's investment arm preparing to exit as a shareholder.

name: Rushd
description: An automated investment platform in Oman, run by Suhaib Aldughaishi Investments, that builds and manages Shariah-compliant portfolios from a client's goals and risk tolerance. In October 2026 it entered a supervised live trial inside Oman's Financial Services Authority sandbox, with no public launch until it earns a final licence. No official company website could be verified.

name: Raya Financing
description: A Saudi finance company offering retail finance, leasing, and auto finance. In October 2026 it selected the Temenos Core banking platform to centralise its operations and prepare new products, including personal finance, small-business lending, buy now pay later services, and home finance.

name: Temenos
description: A banking software firm whose Temenos Core platform records accounts, payments, and financing deals for banks and finance companies. Its configurable setup lets a lender add new products from templates instead of building each one from scratch.

name: Network International
description: A Dubai-based payments company that processes card payments and runs back-office operations for banks and merchants across the Middle East and Africa. In October 2026 it renewed its processing agreement with Emirates Islamic, including real-time data services and an instalment option.

name: Emirates Islamic
description: One of the leading Islamic banks in the United Arab Emirates, offering Shariah-compliant personal, business, and corporate banking. In October 2026 it renewed its card payments processing agreement with Network International as it expands its digital services.

name: Syndicated financing
description: A single large financing shared by several banks. One bank arranges the deal and sets the terms, and other banks join, each taking a share of the facility, so the borrower deals with one agreement instead of negotiating with each bank separately. Example: Digital Nasional Berhad's MYR5.2 billion facility, shared by Maybank Investment Bank, AmInvestment, CIMB Islamic, RHB Islamic, and UOB Malaysia.

name: Regulatory sandbox
description: A supervised trial space where a regulator lets a new financial service run live with real clients under limits, such as caps on client numbers and transaction volumes, while it checks the service before granting a full licence. Example: Oman's Financial Services Authority trial of the Rushd automated advice platform.

name: Payment processing
description: The system that moves a card payment from a shop to the customer's bank. The processor checks the transaction and routes it to the bank, and the back-office work that follows matches payments to accounts, settles the money, and keeps the records straight. Example: Network International processing card payments for Emirates Islamic.

name: MIZAN
description: A core banking platform from Peerless built for Islamic and non-interest banks. Its records follow Islamic contracts directly, including murabaha sales, ijara leases, and mudaraba profit sharing, with profit calculation and audit controls built in. Example: Nigeria's alt bank runs all its banking services on MIZAN.

name: iMAL
description: An AAOIFI-certified Islamic core banking platform from Path Solutions, built for Islamic banks from the start. It covers retail, corporate, and investment banking, including profit calculation, financing, and trade finance. Example: Islamic banks across the Middle East and Africa run on iMAL.

name: Oracle FLEXCUBE
description: A general banking platform from Oracle with a dedicated Islamic banking suite. It runs Islamic products alongside conventional ones, including Islamic windows inside conventional banks, covering products such as murabaha, wakala, and ijara.

name: National Bank of Bahrain
description: Bahrain's first locally owned bank, founded in 1957, and the majority owner of Bahrain Islamic Bank. It offers retail, corporate, and investment banking, and structured the sustainable murabaha deal in this edition together with its Islamic arm.

name: Bahrain Islamic Bank (BisB)
description: Bahrain's first Islamic bank, founded in 1979. It offers Shariah-compliant retail and corporate banking, and applied its Islamic treasury expertise and Sustainable Finance Framework to the murabaha deal in this edition.

name: Abu Dhabi Islamic Bank (ADIB)
description: One of the UAE's largest Islamic banks. It offers Shariah-compliant retail, corporate, and card products, including the co-branded covered cards launched with Aldar in this edition.

name: Aldar Properties
description: Abu Dhabi's leading real estate developer, investor, and manager. It runs the Darna digital loyalty programme across its malls, hotels, schools, and residential communities.

name: Covered card
description: The Shariah-compliant version of a credit card. The bank charges set fees for the card instead of interest on unpaid balances, and earns from the annual fee and the commission merchants pay when the card is used. Example: the ADIB Aldar Visa cards launched in October 2026.

name: Collateralised murabaha
description: A murabaha sale backed by pledged assets as security. The bank buys an asset and sells it at a disclosed markup paid in instalments, and the pledged collateral gives the lender something to fall back on if the borrower cannot pay. Example: NBB Group's sustainable murabaha in Bahrain.

name: International Islamic Trade Finance Corporation (ITFC)
description: The trade finance arm of the Islamic Development Bank group. It finances trade between member countries using Shariah-compliant methods, and advises banks and technology platforms on setting up Shariah-compliant supply chain finance products.

sources.label: Trade Treasury Payments — ITFC puts Islamic finance behind open account trade (Oct 26, 2026)

name: Qualco
description: A Greek technology company whose ProximaPlus platform handles factoring and supply chain finance. In February 2026 its platform was certified to process transactions using Goods Murabaha and Tawarruq structures.

sources.label: Trade Treasury Payments — ITFC puts Islamic finance behind open account trade (Oct 26, 2026)

name: Islamic Development Bank Institute (IsDBI)
description: The research and knowledge arm of the Islamic Development Bank group. In October 2026 it launched Prosper MSMEs with the Universal Postal Union to explore Islamic finance-aligned digital services for small businesses through postal networks.

sources.label: Tripura Star News — IsDBI and UPU launch Prosper MSMEs (Oct 13, 2026)

name: Universal Postal Union (UPU)
description: A United Nations agency, based in Bern, Switzerland, that coordinates postal services across 192 member countries. In October 2026 it partnered with the Islamic Development Bank Institute on Prosper MSMEs, exploring how postal networks can deliver digital financial services to small businesses.

sources.label: Tripura Star News — IsDBI and UPU launch Prosper MSMEs (Oct 13, 2026)

name: Supply chain finance
description: Financing that pays a supplier early for goods already shipped, instead of making the supplier wait until the buyer's payment date. The financier pays the supplier a slightly discounted amount now and collects the full amount from the buyer later. A Shariah-compliant version earns its return through a sale or lease structure, not interest.

sources.label: Trade Treasury Payments — ITFC puts Islamic finance behind open account trade (Oct 26, 2026)

name: Tawarruq
description: A chain of sales used to raise cash without interest. A person buys a commodity on deferred payment, then sells it on for cash and keeps the cash. Each sale is a separate contract, and the cash comes from a real sale of a real commodity.

sources.label: Trade Treasury Payments — ITFC puts Islamic finance behind open account trade (Oct 26, 2026)

name: Factoring
description: Selling unpaid invoices to a company, called a factor, for cash now. The factor pays most of the invoice value within a day or two and collects the full amount from the customer later. For example, a supplier with a $10,000 invoice on 60-day terms might receive $8,500 now and the rest, minus a fee, when the customer pays.

name: Akinda
description: A halal investing platform that screens more than 15,000 stocks in the US, Canada, and the UK against AAOIFI Shariah Standard No. 21, giving each company a clear verdict plus a dividend purification calculator. Its founder moved to the San Francisco Bay Area in fall 2026 to expand into the United States.

sources.label: TechBullion — Akinda takes halal investing global

name: Maybank Islamic
description: Malaysia's largest Islamic bank, part of the Maybank group. It provides Shariah-compliant financing to businesses and consumers, including supply chain financing that pays small suppliers early against approved invoices.

sources.label: Fintech News Malaysia — Maybank Islamic, CGC supply chain financing

name: Credit Guarantee Corporation Malaysia (CGC)
description: A Malaysian guarantee provider, mostly owned by the country's central bank, that promises to cover part of a lender's loss so small businesses without collateral can still get financing. In October 2026 it began guaranteeing mid-tier companies that anchor supply chain financing schemes.

sources.label: Fintech News Malaysia — Maybank Islamic, CGC supply chain financing

name: Open Bank
description: An Uzbek bank that received Uzbekistan's first Islamic banking licence (licence 1-I) in October 2026, allowing it to offer Islamic financial services through an Islamic window under the country's March 2026 Islamic banking law.

sources.label: Spot — Uzbekistan issues first licence for Islamic banking

name: Islamic window
description: A section inside a conventional bank that offers Shariah-compliant services, with its own products, records, and Shariah oversight, while the rest of the bank continues its conventional business. For example, Uzbekistan's Open Bank and Bangladesh's Community Islamic both operate as Islamic windows inside conventional banks.

sources.label: Spot — Uzbekistan issues first licence for Islamic banking

name: Qard Hasan
description: A benevolent loan in Islamic finance. The borrower repays exactly the amount borrowed, with no interest and no extra charge, even if repayment runs late. For example, a community fund lends a shopkeeper money to restock, and she repays it in instalments from her sales.

name: Yield
description: The return earned on money over a year, shown as a percentage. For example, lending $100 and getting $105 back after one year is a 5% yield.

name: Discounting
description: Working out what money promised in the future is worth today. For example, at 5% a year, $1,000 due in three years is worth $863.84 today.

name: SP Wealth Group
description: A wealth group that brings together ShariaPortfolio, SP Funds Management, SP Zero Finance, and ShariaPortfolio Canada, offering Shariah-compliant ETFs and managed portfolios in the United States and Canada. It passed $5 billion in client money in October 2026.

sources.label: GlobeNewswire via The News Headliner, Oct 29, 2026

name: Victoria Capital Management
description: The Mauritius-based investment manager of Perennial, a Shariah-compliant portfolio that invests across stocks, sukuk, and commodities inside the Cayman Islands-based Skye Investment Fund.

name: CUSP Wealth
description: A Dubai-regulated investment platform that offers US stocks and personalised portfolios, including a Shariah-compliant version certified by Amanie Advisors, with screening powered by Zoya.

name: Lion Global Investors
description: A Singapore asset manager, part of the OCBC Group, that runs the LionGlobal Singapore Physical Gold Fund. In October 2026 it added Shariah classes to that fund that can be bought with retirement savings scheme money.

name: Segregated portfolio
description: One legal fund company divided into separate compartments. Each compartment holds its own assets, so the assets of one portfolio are kept apart from the others. For example, Perennial sits as one compartment inside the Skye Investment Fund, with its own share classes and fees.

name: Supplementary Retirement Scheme (SRS)
description: Singapore's voluntary retirement savings scheme. A saver puts money aside for retirement and gets tax relief on contributions. For example, a Singapore saver can use SRS money to buy the Singapore-dollar Islamic class of a physical gold fund.

name: Assets under management (AUM)
description: The total value of client money a firm looks after. For example, SP Wealth Group reported more than $5 billion in assets under management in October 2026, up from $3 billion in December 2025.

name: Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX)
description: Pakistan's national stock exchange, based in Karachi. In October 2026 it opened a Shariah-compliant trading counter where only Shariah-compliant equities and sukuk can trade.

name: Mal
description: A UAE-based Islamic financial platform built around artificial intelligence, founded in 2025. It is still pre-launch, holds no banking licence yet, and opened a global waitlist in September 2026.

name: Murabaha Share Financing (MSF)
description: A way to finance a share purchase without an interest-bearing loan. The financier buys shares and sells them to the investor at a disclosed markup, paid over time. Pakistan's Shariah trading counter offers it as the alternative to conventional margin lending.

name: UAE Ministry of Finance
description: The UAE federal government ministry that manages public finances and issues government debt, including Treasury sukuk and bonds. Example: it issued the October 2026 T-Sukuk auction covered in the Oct 31 edition.

sources.label: UAE Ministry of Finance official site

name: Central Bank of the UAE
description: The UAE's central bank, which manages the dirham currency and banking regulation. Example: it acted as issuing and payment agent for the October 2026 T-Sukuk auction.

sources.label: Central Bank of the UAE official site

name: Nasdaq Dubai
description: An international stock exchange based in Dubai's financial free zone, where sukuk and bonds are listed and traded. Example: the UAE's October 2026 T-Sukuk and T-Bonds are listed there.

name: Treasury sukuk (T-Sukuk)
description: A short- to medium-term sukuk issued by a government to raise money in its own currency. Example: the UAE government sold a T-Sukuk tranche maturing in October 2029 in its October 2026 auction.

name: Cooperative Bank of Oromia
description: An Ethiopian bank whose interest-free banking arm, Coopbank Alhuda, offers Shariah-compliant financing. In October 2026 it launched Michuu-Mizan, a digital platform giving small businesses financing without collateral.

sources.label: Cooperative Bank of Oromia — Michuu-Mizan launch (Oct 30, 2026)

name: Kifiya Financial Technology
description: An Ethiopian financial technology company that builds AI-powered credit scoring and digital lending systems for banks. It partnered with the Cooperative Bank of Oromia on the Michuu-Mizan Shariah-compliant financing platform.

sources.label: Cooperative Bank of Oromia — Michuu-Mizan launch (Oct 30, 2026)

name: AdalFi
description: A Lahore-based digital lending platform that helps partner banks score borrowers from bank transaction data and automate loan approvals. It plans a Rs652 million listing on the Pakistan Stock Exchange to expand Islamic and small-business lending.

name: Initial public offering (IPO)
description: The first sale of a company's shares to the public on a stock exchange. A company issues new shares, investors buy them, and the shares can then be traded on the exchange. AdalFi's planned Rs652 million IPO would make it the first fintech listed on the Pakistan Stock Exchange.

name: MARC Ratings
description: A Malaysian credit rating agency. It grades how likely a borrower is to repay its debt, from strong grades down to C, one step above default, and D, which means payment default.

sources.label: MARC — Zetrix AI rating downgrade to CIS (Oct 30, 2026)

name: Bank Muscat
description: Oman's largest bank. Through its Islamic banking arm Meethaq, it offers Shariah-compliant products, including a money market fund that reopened for regular subscriptions in November 2026 with a minimum investment of RO100.

sources.label: Bank Muscat — Shari'a Money Market Fund

name: Zarea Limited
description: A Lahore-based online marketplace where buyers and sellers trade farm produce and industrial goods such as grain, cement, and steel. It listed on the Pakistan Stock Exchange in February 2025 and uses short-term sukuk to fund the stock it holds for buyers.

sources.label: Mettis Global — Zarea plans Rs3bn rights issue (Nov 2, 2026)

name: PT Pos Indonesia
description: Indonesia's state-owned postal and logistics company, running post offices and agents across the country. Its Tranche I Sukuk was downgraded to default by Fitch in November 2026 after a missed payment.

sources.label: TradersUnion — POS Indonesia sukuk downgraded to default (Nov 3, 2026)

name: Savings Sukuk
description: A government sukuk sold directly to ordinary citizens in small amounts, starting from IDR 1 million in Indonesia. It cannot be traded or transferred to another investor, but the holder can withdraw up to 50% early, and its return moves with the central bank rate subject to a guaranteed minimum.

name: Rights Issue
description: A way for a listed company to raise cash by offering new shares to its existing shareholders first, usually below the market price and in proportion to what they already hold. A shareholder who does not buy sees their percentage ownership fall, which is called dilution.

sources.label: Mettis Global — Zarea plans Rs3bn rights issue (Nov 2, 2026)

name: mamun
description: A Shariah-compliant trade finance platform based in Muscat, Oman. It connects businesses and investors to finance cross-border trade, covering the wait between shipping goods and getting paid, using AI-based checks of the contract, buyer, trade documents, and trading history.

name: International Islamic Liquidity Management Corporation (IILM)
description: An international organisation set up by central banks and monetary authorities, headquartered in Kuala Lumpur. It issues short-term Shariah-compliant sukuk, from two weeks to twelve months, so Islamic banks have a place to manage short-term cash without using interest-bearing instruments.

sources.label: MEA Biz — IILM sets new issuance record with $1.572bn short-term sukuk (Nov 3, 2026)

name: Trade Finance
description: Financing that covers the gap between goods being shipped and payment arriving, often 60 to 90 days later. The financier pays the exporter early or guarantees payment, tied to a specific trade and its documents, and is repaid when the buyer pays.

name: Weststar Aviation Services
description: A Malaysian helicopter operator that flies offshore oil-and-gas crews and government missions such as search and rescue and medical evacuation. In November 2026 it lined up a RM6 billion sukuk to fund 28 helicopters for Malaysian government agencies.

sources.label: MARC Ratings — preliminary AA+IS rating for Weststar Aviation sukuk (Nov 4, 2026)

name: Safaricom
description: Kenya’s largest mobile network operator and the company behind M-Pesa, the mobile money service most Kenyans use to send money. With GulfCap Investment Bank it runs the Ziidi Shari’ah Money Market Fund, which drew 1.5 million customers in its first month.

sources.label: The Eastleigh Voice — Ziidi Shari’ah fund draws 1.5 million users (Nov 5, 2026)

name: GulfCap Investment Bank
description: A Nairobi investment bank licensed by Kenya’s Capital Markets Authority. It runs the Ziidi Shari’ah Money Market Fund with Safaricom, and its Shariah board oversees the fund’s investments.

sources.label: GulfCap Investment Bank — Ziidi Shari’ah Money Market Fund launch
The Eastleigh Voice — Ziidi Shari’ah fund draws 1.5 million users (Nov 5, 2026)

name: Leonardo
description: An Italian aerospace and defence company that builds helicopters used for rescue, medical evacuation, offshore transport and military missions. Its helicopters are the aircraft in Weststar Aviation’s Malaysian government fleet programme.

sources.label: MARC Ratings — preliminary AA+IS rating for Weststar Aviation sukuk (Nov 4, 2026)

name: Project finance
description: Borrowing to build or buy one specific project, where the loan is repaid from the money that project earns. A common example is a government concession: the government pays a company fixed amounts to run a service, and those payments repay the financing.

sources.label: MARC Ratings — preliminary AA+IS rating for Weststar Aviation sukuk (Nov 4, 2026)

name: SITR Compliance Technology
description: A Bahraini regulatory technology startup that builds a platform for Islamic banks to check transactions against their Shariah board's rulings continuously, instead of in periodic samples. It connects to core banking systems through read-only links and reads contracts and scanned documents. No official website could be found; sitrsecure.com is a different company.

name: Medtech Maldives
description: The leading medical equipment and healthcare company in the Maldives, founded in 2009. In November 2026 it raised MVR 80 million through a Parallel Istisna sukuk to build an oceanfront healthcare and commercial complex in Malé.

sources.label: Maaldif — Medtech Maldives seeks MVR 80 million sukuk (Nov 6, 2026)

name: First National Finance Corporation
description: A Maldivian investment firm licensed as a securities dealer and investment adviser. It arranges sukuk and bond issues in the Maldives, including Medtech Maldives' MVR 80 million sukuk in November 2026.

sources.label: Maaldif — Medtech Maldives seeks MVR 80 million sukuk (Nov 6, 2026)
First National Finance Corporation — official website

name: aik by BankIslami
description: Pakistan's first fully digital Islamic banking platform, launched by BankIslami Pakistan Limited. Customers open accounts and use banking services entirely through the aik app, including Shariah-compliant smartphone financing with PalmPay.

sources.label: NationPulse — aik and PalmPay launch smartphone financing (Nov 4, 2026)

name: BankIslami
description: Pakistan's first licensed Islamic bank, established in 2006, with over 540 branches. It launched aik, Pakistan's first fully digital Islamic banking platform.

sources.label: NationPulse — aik and PalmPay launch smartphone financing (Nov 4, 2026)

name: PalmPay
description: A digital financial services company that offers Shariah-compliant smartphone financing in Pakistan on instalments, using the Musawamah model. It holds a buy-now-pay-later licence from Pakistan's Securities and Exchange Commission.

sources.label: NationPulse — aik and PalmPay launch smartphone financing (Nov 4, 2026)

name: Parallel Istisna
description: Two Istisna contracts back to back. In the first, a financier agrees to deliver a finished building to investors; in the second, the financier hires a builder to construct it. Money from the sukuk pays the builder in stages, and the finished building satisfies the first contract. Example: Medtech Maldives' MVR 80 million sukuk to build a healthcare complex in Malé.

sources.label: Maaldif — Medtech Maldives seeks MVR 80 million sukuk (Nov 6, 2026)

name: Shariah audit
description: The check that a bank's transactions followed the rulings of its Shariah board. An internal team reviews transactions after the event, and an external audit reviews that work independently. When a transaction fails the check, the income from it cannot be kept as profit.

name: Musawamah
description: A sale where the buyer and seller agree a price without the seller disclosing what the item cost. The price is fixed in advance and paid in instalments or in full. Example: PalmPay Pakistan's Shariah-compliant smartphone financing.
